title: Search says complete while a declared language has no grammar
body:
Reported by devbin-vc on 2026-09-24, measured by Devbin's cc at 08:36Z on `intent 3.2.0 (4c687eaadbf1)` in Devbin, and passed to Intent with hv's approval. Reproduced by vc in this tree at 09:03Z by `date -u`, on the same pair.

Seen: a project that declares `shell` gets no structural index for its shell files -- `intent index status` reports `grammar: shell no-grammar` -- yet the search envelope answers `"complete": true`, with `skipped` and `stale` empty and `reconciled: true`. So a definition in a shell file reads as ABSENT in an answer that says it is complete:

- here, `intent_search` with `kind=def` and `query=roster_unchecked` answers 0 hits under `"complete": true`, while `git grep` finds `roster_unchecked()` at `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit-guards.sh:121`;
- here, `outline` of that same file answers no symbols under `"complete": true`;
- in Devbin, `kind=def` for `vendored_paths` answers 0 hits while it is defined at `lib/install:258`, and the same holds for outline and context queries on every function under `lib/`.

The control: `kind=def` for `is_claim_address` finds `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/model.rs:201`, so the instrument works where a grammar exists. The CLI's human form of the same shell query prints only its reconcile note and says nothing about the language it cannot see.

Why it matters: the CLAUDE.md Intent generates tells an agent to ask the index before grep and to "fall back to grep only when its answer says the index is not complete for the paths involved". In any project that declares a language with no grammar, that fallback never fires, and the agent reads "no definition" as the answer -- which is also how a Highlander check concludes that nothing of that name exists yet.

Expected: an answer that a file in a declared, grammarless language could have changed says so -- `complete` is false for those paths, or the envelope names the language as unindexed -- and the CLI's human form says it too, so the generated instruction's fallback fires. `author` and `content` also report no-grammar; whether prose languages belong in the structural question is part of the fix, stated rather than assumed.

Ruled: hv, in vc's session on 2026-09-24, received before vc's 09:25Z clock read: "Ok, go with recs." That takes vc's recommendation that this is shipping-grade, so its code half rides 3.2.1. Its doc half -- the generated CLAUDE.md and the MCP server's instructions naming what the index cannot see -- is in the 3.2.1 doc audit either way.

Design ruled (vc under hv's pen, 2026-09-24 09:45Z by `date -u`, answering cc's design before the bank): a language that is not ready counts as unindexed for an answer only the structural tier gives (definitions, references, outline, context and the filter-only door) when the project DECLARES it -- reading only names in `corpus::lang_of`'s own vocabulary, so the prose disciplines `author` and `content` never count -- OR the index holds a file of it within the answer's scope. A `--lang` filter that excludes it drops it from both halves, and an outline is incomplete whenever the outlined file has no language or a not-ready one, and says which. Neither half alone closes this report: `lang_of` maps by file extension only, and Devbin's shell lives in extensionless files under `lib/` and `cmd/` (`lib/install` opens `#!/usr/bin/env bash`), so the files half alone leaves a `--path 'lib/**'` definition query and an outline of `lib/install` answering complete, while the declared half alone would miss a language that is present and undeclared. A text question whose lexical tier ran has read those files' text and stays complete. The envelope gains `unindexed`, a list of language and reason, and `complete` is false while it is non-empty; the CLI's human form and the explorer's freshness note both say it, from one wording in `search.rs`. The doc half adds that the index parses by file extension, so a script without one is invisible to definition, outline and context queries whatever its language.

One addition, measured by cc while building and taken by vc at 09:58Z by `date -u`: `reconcile.rs` `read_content` extracts symbols for DECLARED languages only, so a held file in a language that has a compiled grammar but is not declared is just as blind to definition, outline and context queries. The held half counts it too, with the reason `not-declared`, and the remedy it implies is `intent lang init <lang>`.
